reader.decision: Approve the queued export: move the CSV export to the `documents` queue of `taskq` and email a signed link. Aelita should implement it.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows northfield already needs 240 seconds against a 300-second request limit. Streaming would still hold a gunicorn worker for each export and would break as tenants grow. The queued export removes long work from the request path and reuses existing `taskq`, `storage` and `mailer`.

reconstruction.problem: `export_invoices` builds the whole CSV in memory before sending any byte. For a tenant with 1,840,211 invoices this takes about 240 seconds (18s query plus 222s build). `gw-billing` has `idle_timeout_seconds: 30`, so it returns 504.
reconstruction.what_breaks: The largest tenants never receive a file. The gunicorn worker keeps building after the client has gone. At month end about 900 exports run in two days, which fills all 12 workers (`web_workers_busy=12/12`). `/invoices` p99 rises to 9.4s from 0.4s.
reconstruction.fix: `export_invoices` in `app/exports.py` validates the request, enqueues `render_invoice_csv(tenant_id, recipient)` on the `documents` queue and returns 202. The new task in `jobs/invoice_csv.py` is modelled on `jobs/invoice_pdf.py`. It streams rows into `storage.put`, then calls `storage.signed_url` and `mailer.send` to email a download link.
reconstruction.cost: Users get an email instead of an instant download. Month-end exports may load the `documents` queue, so its capacity needs watching.

reader.closing_answer: I approve the queued export with an emailed signed link. I do not want the streamed response.
